Pennsylvania 2026 resource-adequacy report, Table 11 notes and Table 14 footnote: obtain the complete project-selection ledger and the underlying report of a possible 2031 Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart. Compare the credited summer-2027 date with dated NRC approvals, PJM agreements, required upgrades, and construction milestones.

Independence note: S11 is co-authored by Synapse, which also authored S1; E11 and E178 use the same all-under-construction/90%-engineering-and-procurement rule. Check both reports' model and input provenance before treating A1 and A2 as independent corroboration of project readiness. Different publication titles do not establish independent verification.

PJM January 2025 Load Forecast Report annual tables, including Tab F1, and the October 25, 2024 Load Analysis Subcommittee submissions from Dominion, NOVEC, and ODEC: obtain 2025–2030 annual peak and energy values, coincident-peak definitions, data-centre hourly profiles, project-screening rules, and Northern Virginia delivery-substation allocations, including relevant APS territory.

PJM 2025 ELCC/RRS Table 4 and its underlying vendor resource portfolios: obtain unit-level additions, retirements, retention alternatives, storage durations, accredited capacity, and import assumptions. Reconcile these with the fleet operating on December 31, 2024, rather than treating total modeled ICAP or UCAP as an internal-generation ledger.

Obtain an annual 2025–2030 counterfactual reliability run using the January 2025 forecast that explicitly prohibits post-baseline fuel-burning additions, uprates, and behind-the-meter additions. Report accredited margins, LOLE, and unserved energy with chronological storage limits and stressed weather; compare planned retirements against retention and on-time projects against delays. Existing S1 and S11 results include new gas and cannot supply this comparison directly.

PJM RTEP and Dominion transmission-planning studies for Northern Virginia through 2030: obtain named interfaces, reinforcement need dates, contingency violations and margins with and without each critical reinforcement, and delayed-project cases identifying required connection deferrals or load limits. Separate these findings from PJM-wide adequacy.

For the restricted counterfactual, obtain firm-import contracts and transmission rights identifying external generator fuel and commissioning dates, plus executed Northern Virginia data-centre interruption agreements specifying MW, hours, notice, duration, recovery demand, and backup-generation use. Test feasibility with and without these resources and with dispatchable storage included in the prohibition.
